findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses && instead of ||
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. That requires the user to be both admin and owner, so in practice only owners pass. Plain team admins cannot add guests to team bookings, even though the variable name and intent say they should. Use `||`.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's
findings.body: The EventManager is built from `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. The caller may be an attendee or a team admin rather than the organizer. In that case `updateCalendarAttendees` runs against the caller's calendar credentials, not the booking owner's. The organizer's calendar event is then not updated, and the call may fail or touch the wrong calendar. Build the EventManager from `booking.user` and its credentials instead. This call is also outside any try/catch and runs after the DB insert, so a calendar failure surfaces as an error even though the attendees were already persisted.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive
findings.body: The blacklist entries are lowercased, but each `guest` is compared without lowercasing. Existing attendee emails are also compared with strict equality. Entering `Blocked@Domain.com` bypasses `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`, and a different casing of an existing attendee's email creates a duplicate attendee. Normalize all emails to lowercase before comparing.

findings.title: Emails are sent for the raw guest list, not the filtered unique guests
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the original input instead of `uniqueGuests`. If the request includes an email that is already an attendee, that existing attendee is treated as new and gets a full AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the 'guests added' notice. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

findings.title: Server does not dedupe guests within the request
findings.body: Only the client enforces that the submitted emails are unique. The server schema accepts duplicates, and the handler filters only against existing attendees. A direct API call with repeated emails inserts duplicate attendee rows through `createMany`. Dedupe server-side, for example by passing the lowercased list through a Set.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's email-disable settings
findings.body: Every other booking email sender checks `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` against the event type metadata. This new function takes no metadata and always emails the organizer, team members and every attendee. Event types configured to suppress standard emails will still send them when guests are added.

findings.title: No check on booking state before adding guests
findings.body: The handler only checks permissions. It does not reject cancelled, rejected or past bookings. It also does not respect the event type's guests booking-field configuration, for example when guests are hidden or disabled. Guests can therefore be added, and invitations sent, for bookings that should not accept them.

findings.title: Error toast fallback is unreachable and can show 'undefined:'
findings.body: `message` is a template string, so it is always truthy and the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback is never used. When `err.data` is absent, the toast reads 'undefined: ...'.

findings.title: Invalid-email error state is never cleared after edits or success
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true on a failed validation. It is cleared only by the Cancel button. Correcting the emails, a successful submission, or closing the dialog via overlay or Escape (`onOpenChange`) leaves the error banner visible the next time the dialog opens.
